title: The Cotton Club shows bored him
summary: He found rehearsing the Cotton Club shows tedious, though the band played plenty behind acts such as the Berry Brothers.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's quite right. Well, okay. Well,

listen, then, let's go back to being with Duke, which was at the Cotton Club. And I tell you, I was thinking about those records. Those early Ellington records. And we were saying, after all, he didn't really feature people the same way then. They were three minute records. But there were records that sort of introduced you to the Ellington public, you know. And all of those -- when we do this again, we'll just mention those titles. Because you don't really remember them, do you?
No. I don't.
No.
Not the first records.
Because, as you say, Bubber made East St. Louis. You made it later. But he made the first one.
Yeah.
Well, okay. So we'll go -- the next time we do this, I'll have that information. So, the Cotton Club. Well, did you get a kick out of that show at all? Any of those shows at the Cotton Club?
No.
(Laughter)
You still only had your mind on the trumpet?
That's right.
Isn't that funny. Well, what about -- I mean, none of those dancers or --
No. The shows used to bore me.
They did.
Well, after rehearsing those shows all day long and day after day, day after day, they got real boring.
Yes. Well, that's right. Because there wasn't much room in there for anybody to blow anything.
No. No room at all.
And there were like three shows a night, I think. Am I right? Or at least two, weren't there.
Something like that, yeah.
And so there wasn't -- the most it would be would be two band sets in between shows, I think.
Yeah.
Not much more, was there.
Not much more.
And then maybe one more to close off.
Yeah.
So you really didn't get to do an awful lot of blowing.
Oh, we blowed a lot. We blowed during that show.
Oh, well, yeah.
During that show.
Oh. Well, yeah, there were -- I mean
there were dance acts and things you could blow behind, weren't there?
Not particularly in jazz.
No?
No.
There weren't people like the Berry Brothers or the Nicholas Brothers, people like that, huh?
The Berry Brothers, but you had to play their act. They had music and you had to play their music.
Yeah. I guess in those two years, it was Ethel Waters and Stormy Weather, wasn't it?
Yeah. That's right.
And then, isn't that the show when they had -- or maybe was that later on -- when Duke had written "Let a Song Go Out of My Heart", and they threw it out?
I don't remember that.
I think that must be later, "Let a Song Go Out of My Heart", don't you?
Maybe so, yeah.
I don't think that was back in the '30s, was it. '31 or '32.
No. Because that was the band. You know, the bigger band.
